planting.note: Plant container-grown Tequila Sunrise in spring once nights stay reliably above the mid-20s F, since this Coprosma repens selection is hardy only in mild coastal climates; it needs sharply drained soil and full sun to color up fully.

directions: Site this patented mirror plant where its glossy leaves can catch the light, since the foliage show is the entire point of growing it. New growth emerges emerald and gold, then shifts through orange-gold to a deep orange-and-red as leaves mature, giving the shrub several color zones at once. Keep it in fast-draining soil and let it dry between waterings once established, as soggy roots are its main vulnerability. It tolerates deer, salt spray, and light pruning well, making it a good low-fuss choice for borders, slopes, and large containers in mild-winter gardens.

common_name: DownHome Harvest Hello Darlin Blueberry (Low-Chill Early-Fruiting Southern Highbush Blueberry)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container stock in late winter to early spring in acidic, well-drained soil amended with peat or pine bark; this University of Florida low-chill release fruits earliest when a second low-chill blueberry variety is planted nearby for cross-pollination.

directions: Grow in full sun in acidic soil (pH 4.5-5.5) with consistent moisture, mulching with pine bark or needles to keep roots cool and the root zone acidic. This University of Florida-bred selection was chosen for its early, heavy fruit set and low chill-hour requirement, making it a reliable backyard blueberry for mild-winter southern gardens where many northern-bred varieties fail to set fruit. Plant alongside a second early-season low-chill variety to boost pollination and yield. Expect spring flowers followed by a concentrated early harvest the first full season after establishment.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring or fall in well-drained garden soil; this Suntastic-series Abelia stays naturally compact, so it needs little pruning or fertilizer to perform in borders, low hedges, or containers.

directions: Grow in full coastal sun to partial shade in hotter inland climates, in well-drained garden soil with moderate water until established. The bright peach-toned variegated foliage holds its color through the growing season and needs little intervention to look tidy, since this patented Suntastic-series selection was bred specifically to stay compact without regular shearing. Summer brings small tubular flowers that draw pollinators, adding a second season of interest to the colorful foliage display. Use it as a low hedge, foundation planting, or container specimen where its naturally dense habit can be appreciated up close.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring or fall in well-drained garden soil; like its Suntastic-series siblings, this selection stays compact on its own and needs little to no fertilizer or regular pruning.

directions: Site in full sun to partial shade in well-drained soil, watering regularly until roots establish and then tapering to moderate water. This patented Suntastic-series Abelia keeps a naturally dense, rounded shape, which makes it a low-maintenance substitute for standard glossy abelia in borders and low hedges. Small flowers open in summer and attract bees and butterflies, adding bloom interest on top of the colorful year-round foliage. If it ever gets leggy, a light shearing in early spring before new growth flushes will restore its compact form.

common_name: Indigo Frost Agapanthus (Bicolor White-and-Blue Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full coastal sun to part shade inland; this compact, deciduous agapanthus is more cold-sensitive than evergreen types, so mulch the crown where winter lows approach 5 to 10 F.

directions: Grow in full coastal sun to partial shade in hotter climates, in well-drained soil, and let the ground dry between waterings once the clump is established since this patented selection is marketed as water-wise. Multiple spikes of large bicolor white-and-blue flowers rise above the clumping foliage in summer, making it a strong cut-flower and border candidate. The deciduous habit means foliage dies back in winter, so plant it where a dormant gap won't leave a hole in the design. It tolerates heat and resists most pests and diseases, and works well massed, in containers, or along edging.

common_name: Ever Twilight Agapanthus (Chelsea Flower Show Award Bicolor Dwarf Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full coastal sun to part shade inland; this dwarf, reblooming agapanthus stays under two feet tall, so it suits tight borders and container plantings where larger agapanthus would overwhelm the space.

directions: Grow this dwarf evergreen agapanthus in full coastal sun to partial shade inland, in well-drained soil with low water once roots are established. Large bicolor white-and-violet blooms open on short 16 to 18 inch stalks from spring into summer and continue in flushes rather than a single bloom period. This patented selection won recognition at the 2019 Chelsea Flower Show for its compact habit and flower quality, and it holds up well as a cut flower. Use it in mass plantings, mixed borders, or containers where its tidy clumping form and drought tolerance make it easy to maintain.
